name: Tax
takeaways: Categories are org-wide; rates are per entity
Tax categories can be renamed but never deleted

cards.title: Tax category
cards.body: Classifies how a product is taxed. Defined once for the organization. It can be renamed but never deleted.

cards.title: Third-party tax code
cards.body: Each category can map to one code per third-party engine. The engine receives only the code, not the category. Zenskar does not translate codes between engines.
cards.example: SaaS subscription maps to Avalara code SW054000.

cards.title: Business entity config
cards.body: Each entity has its own served countries, tax engines and rates. Rates of one entity never apply to another.
cards.example: US entity and German entity configured separately.

cards.title: Served country
cards.body: A country where the entity bills customers, taken from the customer's billing address. It needs at least one currency and covers a contract only if the contract currency is listed.

cards.title: Tax engine
cards.body: The Zenskar engine or one connected third-party engine (Avalara AvaTax or Anrok) per served country. An entity connects at most one third-party engine and may mix engines across countries.
cards.example: Avalara for the US, Zenskar engine for India.

cards.title: Zenskar tax engine
cards.body: The organization maintains rates. Rate depends on category and the customer billing address matched to jurisdictions.
cards.example: 8% for category X in jurisdiction Y.

cards.title: Rates over time
cards.body: A rate belongs to one category and one jurisdiction and changes through dated rate changes made of tax components.

cards.title: Third-party engine
cards.body: Zenskar sends the tax code and both addresses. The engine applies its own rates and rules and records transactions for filing.

edgeCases: Missing code. A category without a code for a connected engine can affect contracts. Zenskar does not check the mapping when an engine is switched.
Removing a country. It takes effect immediately with no confirmation. Rates are kept.
Disconnected engine. Served countries keep it, shown as (not connected). Codes stay but are hidden.
Missing rates. The entity card shows N countries need rates when the Zenskar engine has none for a served country.
Ambiguous rates. The resolve-rate API returns 422 when several rows match, 404 when none do. Close one row or deactivate it.
Exemption. Customer tax exemption comes from a custom attribute you define.
Two engines. An organization using two third-party engines connects each to a different entity.

quiz.question: Can you delete a tax category?
quiz.explanation: Renaming is the way to retire one.

quiz.question: What does a third-party engine receive?
options: The third-party tax code and both addresses
quiz.explanation: The category itself is not sent.

quiz.question: How many third-party engines can one entity connect?
quiz.explanation: Mixing is across countries, using the Zenskar engine or the one connected engine.

quiz.question: When does a served country cover a contract?
options: When the contract currency is on its list
quiz.explanation: Every billing currency must be listed.

qa.question: Tax category vs tax code?
qa.answer: A category is Zenskar's classification. A tax code is the third-party engine's identifier mapped to it.

qa.question: Zenskar engine vs Avalara vs Anrok?
qa.answer: With the Zenskar engine your organization maintains rates. Avalara and Anrok apply their own rates and rules.

qa.question: Business entity tax config vs organization tax categories?
qa.answer: Categories are organization-wide; served countries, engines and rates are per entity.

qa.question: Served country vs customer country?
qa.answer: A served country is where the entity bills. The customer's billing address decides which applies.

qa.question: Tax rate vs rate change vs component?
qa.answer: A rate belongs to a category and jurisdiction, changes over time through dated rate changes, and is made of components.

qa.question: Resolve-rate 404 vs 422?
qa.answer: 404 means no rate matches; 422 means several rows match and the configuration is ambiguous.

qa.question: Disconnected vs removed engine?
qa.answer: Disconnecting keeps the country mapped but marks it (not connected). Removing a served country takes effect immediately.

qa.question: Sell SaaS and services with different tax?
qa.answer: Create two categories and assign one per product.

qa.question: Bill in Canada in CAD and USD?
qa.answer: Add Canada as a served country with both currencies.

qa.question: Use Avalara in the US and Zenskar engine in India?
qa.answer: Choose an engine per served country, within one third-party engine per entity.

qa.question: Tax-exempt customer?
qa.answer: Use a customer custom attribute.

qa.question: Check what rate applies on a date?
qa.answer: Call resolve applicable rate with category, destination and date.

qa.question: Can I delete a tax category?
qa.answer: No. It can only be renamed.

qa.question: A product category lacks a code for the engine?
qa.answer: Contracts can be affected, and Zenskar does not check mapping when an engine changes.

qa.question: Does Zenskar translate codes between engines?
qa.answer: No.

qa.question: What if no rates exist for a served country?
qa.answer: The entity card shows N countries need rates.

qa.question: Can a country change after being added?
qa.answer: No.

qa.question: A contract's currency is not on the country's list?
qa.answer: The country does not cover that contract.

qa.question: Two third-party engines in one entity?
qa.answer: Not allowed. Connect each to a different entity.

qa.question: What does Avalara receive?
qa.answer: The third-party tax code plus both addresses, not the category.
